summary: Tested Web Push punch reminders, the reminder crons, the redesigned credential slip and the new admin password. Backend pytest /app/backend/tests/test_push_reminders.py: 18/18 pass. Checks: admin login works with Arun2023@12 and the old WorkPulse@2026 fails; push public-key; subscribe, status, test and unsubscribe for a TEST employee (upsert is idempotent; push/test with a fake FCM subscription returns {sent:int} with no 500); invalid subscriptions (http endpoint, missing keys or missing auth) return 400; admin gets 403; no token gets 401. Cron punch-reminder-in/out: no or wrong Bearer returns 401; unknown kind returns 404; replies {accepted:true} in under 5s; reminder_logs gets a record with finished_at; a repeated X-Webhook-Id returns duplicate:true. crons.yml contract holds. sw.js has push and notificationclick handlers; manifest is valid. Targeting logic was tested at method level by patching push_to_user and using 4 TEST employees: 'in' reached only the employee with no punch; 'out' reached only the employee punched in but not out; the employee on approved leave and the one fully punched were skipped. UI checks: the slips dialog opens with 0 of 11 selected and Generate disabled. Choosing only the TEST employee gives 'Generate 1 slip(s)'. window.confirm appears, and Cancel leaves the dialog open with nothing reset. Accept shows the preview with 1 slip: dark box (rgb 15,23,42), short code AE0955 at 36px, an 8-character password, a QR svg (value is origin/login), install instructions and the portal URL. Employee dashboard (390px and 1920px): the Punch reminders panel renders. Headless Chromium reports Notification.permission=denied (grant_permissions had no effect), so it correctly shows 'Notifications are blocked...' with the button disabled. No page errors and no horizontal overflow. The service worker /sw.js is registered. Real subscribe/test/off from the UI could not be run because permission is denied in headless. Real employees untouched (no slip_issued_at); all TEST data, subscriptions and reminder_logs removed.

minor.issue: Idempotency race: the reminder_logs record for run_id is inserted inside the background task. Two deliveries of the same X-Webhook-Id arriving almost together can both pass the duplicate check and both send. Insert the log record (or use a unique index on run_id) before spawning the task.
Holidays are not considered; only Sunday is excluded by the cron. Reminders will also go out on company holidays.

ui_bugs.issue: The ON/OFF state comes only from the browser's pushManager.getSubscription(), not from the server (/api/push/status). (a) If the server deleted the subscription (404/410) or it belongs to another user, the UI still shows ON. (b) On a shared phone, after user A logs out and user B logs in, B sees ON while the server subscription is still tied to A. B gets no reminders and A's reminders appear on B's phone. Logout does not unsubscribe. Suggestion: on mount, if a browser subscription exists, re-POST /push/subscribe (upsert moves it to the current user) or check /push/status; on logout, call /push/unsubscribe.

action_items: PunchReminders: sync the browser subscription with the server for the current user on mount, and unsubscribe on logout (shared-device bug).
Cron reminder: insert the run_id log before spawning the background task, or add a unique index, to close the duplicate race.
Optional: skip reminders on company holidays.
critical_code_review_comments: push_to_user sends to each subscription in turn via to_thread. Fine for about 10 employees; with hundreds, use asyncio.gather with a semaphore.
Fake/expired subscriptions: 404/410 removes them; other errors only log a warning, so an invalid sub returning 400/403 stays forever. Consider deleting after N failures.
The QR encodes window.location.origin, so slips printed from the preview URL point to preview. Print from the production domain.
The test file lives in /app/backend/tests, so the backend hot reload restarts when it is edited (harmless).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of testable flows (push enable/test/off not testable headless: permission denied)
